q: Which of the following clients should the nurse delegate the taking of vital signs for to the unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP)?
o: A client being prepared for elective facial surgery with a history of stable hypertension.
A client receiving a blood transfusion with a history of transfusion reactions.
A client recently started on a new antiarrhythmic agent.
A client who is admitted frequently with asthma attacks.
r:
Correct: “A client being prepared for elective facial surgery with a history of…” – The client is stable.

Not correct:
• “A client receiving a blood transfusion with a history of transfusion…” – This client is unstable.
• “A client recently started on a new antiarrhythmic agent” – The UAP cannot take apical pulses.
• “A client who is admitted frequently with asthma attacks” – This client is unstable and vital sign measurement should not be delegated.

q: Which of the following medical asepsis actions should the nurse take to reduce and prevent the spread of microorganisms? Select all that apply.
o: Practicing hand hygiene.
Reapplying a sterile dressing.
Sterilizing contaminating items.
Applying a sterile gown and gloves.
Routinely cleaning the hospital environment.
Wearing clean gloves to prevent direct contact with blood or body fluids.
r:
Correct:
• “Practicing hand hygiene” – This is not a sterile procedure.
• “Routinely cleaning the hospital environment” – This is not a sterile procedure.
• “Wearing clean gloves to prevent direct contact with blood or body flu…” – This is not a sterile procedure.

Not correct:
• “Reapplying a sterile dressing” – This is a sterile procedure.
• “Sterilizing contaminating items” – This is a sterile procedure.
• “Applying a sterile gown and gloves” – This is a sterile procedure.

(From your class slides.)

q: The nurse is caring for a client with a decubitus ulcer (stage 4). The wound culture result shows MRSA in the wound bed. Which type of transmission-based precautions should the nurse institute?
o: Standard.
Droplet.
Contact.
Airborne.
r:
Correct: “Contact” – MRSA in a wound indicates contact isolation.

Not correct:
• “Standard” – Although they are used for all clients, standard precautions would not help decrease the spread of MRSA.
• “Droplet” – MRSA in the nares would indicate droplet isolation.
• “Airborne” – This isolation is indicated for very small molecules that linger for long periods in the air.

q: The nurse is triaging clients involved in a mass causality disaster using the color-coded tagging system. Which clients should be tagged red? Select all that apply.

Has chest pain.

q: The nurse is caring for a client prescribed 2 units of packed red blood cells. Which of the following actions should the nurse implement when caring for the client. Select all that apply.
o: Verify that the ABO and Rh of the 2 units are the same.
Infuse a unit of PRBCs in less than 4 hours.
Stop the transfusion if a reaction occurs but keep the line open.
Take the vital signs every 15 minutes while the unit is transfusing.
Inspect the blood bag for leaks, abnormal color, and clots.
Use a 22-gauge catheter for optimal flow of a blood transfusion.
r:
Correct:
• “Infuse a unit of PRBCs in less than 4 hours” – A unit should infuse in 4 hours or less.
• “Stop the transfusion if a reaction occurs but keep the line open” – If a reaction occurs you should stop the infusion and KVO.
• “Inspect the blood bag for leaks, abnormal color, and clots” – Blood should be inspected for these prior to administration.

Not correct:
• “Verify that the ABO and Rh of the 2 units are the same” – You need to verify units with the client's identifier information not the bags.
• “Take the vital signs every 15 minutes while the unit is transfusing” – Vitals should be taken prior to administration, every 15 minutes for the first hour, then every hour until complete. Not every 15 minutes for the entire transfusion.
• “Use a 22-gauge catheter for optimal flow of a blood transfusion” – A 19 gauge or larger catheter should be used so RBCs are not destroyed by the lumen.

q: The nurse is caring for a multiple gunshot victim. Which of the following actions should the nurse take to properly secure and handle legal evidence? Select all that apply. Place bags on the hands and feet.
o: Place paper bags on the hands and feet
Give clothing and wallet to the family.
Cut clothing along the seams, avoiding bullet holes.
Collect all personal items, including items from clothing pockets.
Place wet clothing and personal belongings in a labeled, sealed plastic bag.
Do not allow family members, significant others, or friends to be alone with the client.
r:
Correct:
• “Place paper bags on the hands and feet” – Need to preserve evidence.
• “Cut clothing along the seams, avoiding bullet holes” – Forensics will need to test the bullet hole areas.
• “Collect all personal items, including items from clothing pockets” – It will all need listed for potential evidence.
• “Do not allow family members, significant others, or friends to be alo…” – They could tamper with evidence.

Not correct:
• “Give clothing and wallet to the family” – This might be needed for evidence in future.
• “Place wet clothing and personal belongings in a labeled, sealed plast…” – This could harm the evidence if placed with wet items. They should be placed separately, labeled, and sealed.

q: The nurse is caring for a client with borderline personality disorder. The client tells the nurse “you are the best nurse here; the others just want a paycheck.” Which of the following responses by the nurse is appropriate?
o: “Thank you, you are a nice person.”
“All of the nurses here provide good care.”
“Other clients have told me that also.”
“Have you had problems with other nurses?”
r:
Correct: ““All of the nurses here provide good care.”” – This stops the client from ‘splitting’ the nurses.

Not correct:
• ““Thank you, you are a nice person.”” – The nurse needs to understand the client is using splitting behavior and respond with a neutral comment.
• ““Other clients have told me that also.”” – The nurse needs to understand the client is using splitting behavior and respond with a neutral comment.
• ““Have you had problems with other nurses?”” – The nurse needs to understand the client is using splitting behavior and respond with a neutral comment.

q: Which of the following medication amounts is appropriate for a client who is being treated with imipramine on an outpatient basis for recurring depression and suicidal ideation to have prescribed?

Correct: “7-day supply” – This medication amount would not allow the client to overdose if taken in its entirety.

Not correct:
• “30-day supply” – This medication is lethal in overdose and the client has suicidal ideation. A 30-day supply would allow them access to potentially overdose.
• “21-day supply” – This medication is lethal in overdose and the client has suicidal ideation. A 21-day supply would allow them access to potentially overdose.
• “14-day supply” – This medication is lethal in overdose and the client has suicidal ideation. A 14-day supply would allow them access to potentially overdose.

q: A paranoid client reports that men in blue clothing keep looking in the window and whispering. Which of the following responses by the nurse is most appropriate?
o: “Those men are groundskeepers. They are talking about their work, not you.”
“Do not take things personally, not everyone who is whispering is whispering about you.”
“Do not pay attention to the men. Shall we play cards instead.”
“I will close the drapes so you can't see the men.”
r:
Correct: ““Those men are groundskeepers. They are talking about their work, not…” – The nurse does not want to agree with the client. They should be truthful and matter of fact.

Not correct:
• ““Do not take things personally, not everyone who is whispering is whi…” – This disregards the clients thought and appears condescending.
• ““Do not pay attention to the men. Shall we play cards instead.”” – This is distraction and the client will still have the same thoughts.
• ““I will close the drapes so you can't see the men.”” – This does not address the false thoughts of the client.

q: The nurse is working at an osteoporosis screening clinic. Which of the following female clients is at greatest risk for developing osteoporosis? Select all that apply.

Correct:

• “A female who started menopause early” – Menopause predisposes females to osteoporosis.

• “A female with a family history of osteoporosis” – Calcium and vitamin D deficiency are associated with osteoporosis.

Not correct:
• “A large framed, dark-skinned female” – Its common in small framed females.
• “A female who has a physically active lifestyle” – Those with a sedentary lifestyle are prone to osteoporosis.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who asks the nurse to witness an advance directive. Which of the following actions should the nurse implement?
o: Decline the client’s request politely.
Agree to sign the document as a witness.
Notify the PHCP of the client's request.
Help the client locate an unrelated third party.
r:
Witnesses to an advance directive should be impartial: not a relative, not an heir or beneficiary, and in many states not an employee of the care facility or the treating provider. The nurse supports the client’s autonomy by helping find an appropriate witness (an unrelated third party) rather than refusing or signing. State rules vary, so follow facility policy.

q: The nurse needs to witness the signature on informed consent forms for multiple clients. Which of the following clients are legally able to sign a consent form for surgery? Select all that apply.
o: 16-year-old married client scheduled for a C-Section.
59-year-old client who speaks Spanish only.
30-year-old client who just received amoxicillin.
88-year-old client who is blind but alert and oriented.
17-year-old client who needs emergency appendectomy.
r:
Correct:
• 16-year-old married client – an emancipated minor (married under 18) can consent.
• 30-year-old who received amoxicillin – an antibiotic does not impair the ability to give consent.
• 88-year-old who is blind but alert and oriented – a disability that does not affect comprehension does not remove the right to sign.

Not correct:
• Spanish-only speaker – needs an interpreter before consent is informed.
• 17-year-old needing an appendectomy – a minor who is not emancipated needs a parent or guardian (emergencies may proceed under implied consent).

q: The nurse is discussing living wills with a client. The client asks the nurse if a living will, prepared 3 years ago, remains in effect. Which response should the nurse provide to the client?
o: “Yes, a living will never expire.”
“You need to speak to an attorney.”
“I will call someone to answer your question.”
“It is recommended to review them yearly and update with your health care provider.”
r:
A living will stays valid until the client changes it, but it should be reviewed regularly (about yearly) and updated with the provider as health and wishes change. The nurse gives accurate teaching directly instead of deflecting to an attorney or another person.

q: The nurse is teaching nursing staff about computerized documentation. Which of the following information should the nurse include?
o: Document pain findings within the hour of assessment.
Promote care continuity by using standardized care plans.
Omit narrative progress notes for clinical condition changes.
Use predefined statements for abnormal findings while charting by exception.
r:
Electronic records support continuity of care through standardized care plans that every discipline can see. Charting by exception uses predefined statements for NORMAL findings, and abnormal findings and condition changes still require narrative notes, so the other options are wrong.

q: The nurse in the outpatient clinic is talking with a 22-year-old client who is seeking treatment for constipation and given a prescription and discharge instructions for bisacodyl therapy. Which of the following statements by the client would require follow-up? Select all that apply.
o: “I should drink 2 to 4 glasses of water per day.”
“I will take the medication on an empty stomach to obtain quick relief from constipation.”
“I will notify my health care provider if I should experience abdominal pain without any relief.”
“I should make sure that I do not take the medication with an antacid even to prevent gastric upset.”
“I should plan on taking the medication for the rest of my life to prevent any future episodes of discomfort.”
r:
Bisacodyl is a stimulant laxative for short-term use. Follow-up is needed for: drinking only 2–4 glasses of water (the client should take in about 8–10 glasses a day to help the laxative work and prevent dehydration) and planning to use it for life (long-term use causes dependence and electrolyte loss). Taking it on an empty stomach, reporting unrelieved abdominal pain, and avoiding antacids (they dissolve the enteric coating early) are all correct.

q: The nurse and unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) are caring for an agitated client who had physical restraints applied 5 minutes ago. Which of the following interventions would be appropriate for the nurse to assign to the UAP?
o: Assessing the client’s behavior.
Monitoring the client’s orientation level.
Providing range-of-motion exercises for the client.
Deciding whether or not to remove the client’s restraints.
r:
UAPs may perform routine, stable tasks such as range of motion and basic care. Assessment, monitoring mental status, and the decision to remove restraints require the RN’s judgment and cannot be delegated.

q: The nurse is caring for a group of assigned clients on the medical surgical unit. Which of the following clients should the nurse see first?
o: Client with a spinal cord injury who is flushed, diaphoretic.
Client with diabetes mellitus (type 2) who has a finger stick glucose level of 242 mg/dL.
Client with hyperparathyroidism with a calcium level of 11.5 mg/dL.
Client with angina complaining of a headache after receiving prescribed nitroglycerin.
r:
A flushed, diaphoretic client with a spinal cord injury suggests autonomic dysreflexia, a life-threatening emergency (severe hypertension, risk of stroke). The glucose of 242, calcium of 11.5, and a nitroglycerin headache are expected or only mildly abnormal and can wait.

q: The nurse in the outpatient clinic is talking with a 42-year-old client who has hypertension and is receiving a loop diuretic. Which of the following statements by the client would require follow-up? Select all that apply.
o: “I should still follow my low-sodium diet.”
“I will stand slowly from a seated position.”
“I will increase my fluid intake each day to 5L.”
“I should weight myself once a month.”
“I will take the medication at the same time of the day, every day.”
r:
Requires follow-up: drinking 5 L a day (fluid should not be pushed excessively and should be guided by the provider) and weighing once a month (diuretic clients should weigh daily to track fluid loss or gain). Low-sodium diet, standing slowly to prevent orthostatic hypotension, and a consistent daily dosing time are correct.

q: The nurse in the emergency department is caring for a 9-year-old client with asthma. Client reports chest tightness with cough especially at night for 2 evenings. Expiratory wheeze throughout the chest. T 98.6 °F, P 110, RR 28, SpO2 89% on room air. Sitting in tripod position. The nurse should first:
o: apply humidified supplemental oxygen at 2L/min via nasal cannula
ask parent about allergens in the home
remind the client how to use metered dose inhaler
check the client’s peak flow with a peak expiratory flow meter
r:
Airway, breathing, circulation: SpO2 of 89%, tachypnea, wheezing, and tripod positioning show hypoxemia and respiratory distress, so oxygen is first. Allergen history, inhaler teaching, and peak flow come after the client is stabilized (peak flow is also hard to do in acute distress).

q: The nurse in the outpatient clinic is caring for a 40-year-old client that is taking an ACE inhibitor. Which actions are indicated for this client? Select all that apply.
o: Teach the client to report if a dry cough occurs
Teach the client that the medication should be taken without food.
Advise the client to increase potassium intake.
Female clients who become pregnant should immediately notify the provider.
r:
ACE inhibitors commonly cause a dry cough (report it, the drug may need changing) and are teratogenic, so pregnancy must be reported at once. They cause potassium retention, so clients should NOT increase potassium intake, and most can be taken with or without food.

q: A client is post-operative day 4 after an appendectomy. Which findings indicate the client is NOT progressing as expected? Select all that apply.
o: Can ambulate in the corridor 2 times a day with minimal assistance.
Jackson-Pratt drain has minimal drainage of 15 mL/day.
Refusing to use the incentive spirometer because it causes too much pain.
Using the client-controlled analgesia (PCA) device as ordered.
States no nausea or vomiting.
Abdominal incision dressing is clean, dry, and intact.
Redness and edema noted at the incision site.
r:
Not progressing: refusing the incentive spirometer (risk of atelectasis and pneumonia, so pain control and teaching are needed) and redness and edema at the incision (possible early wound infection). The rest are expected recovery findings.

q: A 72-year-old client on furosemide doubled the dose to catch up and now is drowsy, confused, weak, with numbness and tingling in the hands. ABG: pH 7.48, PaCO2 44 mm Hg, HCO3 30 mEq/L. Which acid-base imbalance is the client most likely experiencing?
o: Metabolic acidosis.
Respiratory acidosis.
Metabolic alkalosis.
Respiratory alkalosis.
r:
pH 7.48 is alkalotic. The HCO3 of 30 is high (normal 22–28) and PaCO2 of 44 is normal, so the cause is metabolic. Excess loop diuretic loses H+, K+ and fluid, producing metabolic alkalosis.

q: The client on furosemide has metabolic alkalosis after taking a doubled dose. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
o: Check the client’s skin turgor.
Assess the client’s electrolyte value pattern.
Ask the client if salt is added to their food at mealtimes.
Have the client describe typical daily bowel and bladder habits.
r:
Overuse of furosemide can cause hypokalemia, hypocalcemia, and hyponatremia, which explain the weakness, confusion, and tingling. Reviewing the electrolyte pattern directly identifies life-threatening imbalances first. Skin turgor and history questions are lower priority.

q: A 26-year-old primigravida client at 4 weeks gestation arrives at the outpatient clinic for an initial prenatal visit. Which of the following findings would be consistent with the client’s history? Select all that apply.
o: Fatigue.
Nausea.
Quickening.
Breast sensitivity.
Braxton Hicks contractions.
r:
Early pregnancy (presumptive signs) includes fatigue, nausea, and breast tenderness. Quickening is first felt around 16–20 weeks (earlier in multiparas), and Braxton Hicks contractions appear in the second and third trimesters.

q: The nurse in the pediatric clinic is caring for a 6-year-old client with recurrent group A streptococcal pharyngitis and inflammation of the conjunctivae. The eyelids are edematous. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
o: Moisten a clean compress with warm water.
Remind the client to avoid rubbing their eyes.
Instill newly prescribed antibiotic drops in both eyes.
Wipe each client eye beginning at the inner canthus.
r:
Crusted drainage must be softened and removed before medication can reach the eye, so the nurse first prepares a warm, moist compress. Then wipe from the inner to the outer canthus with a clean area of cloth for each eye, instill drops, and teach not to rub the eyes.

q: The community health nurse is preparing to host a seminar about preventive care at the local church. Which of the following information should the nurse include for the seminar?
o: Family planning and well-baby care.
Adult screening for blood pressure and cholesterol.
Family focused medical home and ambulatory care.
Rehabilitative programs such as sports medicine and orthopedic.
r:
Preventive care is the primary level of health care, which focuses on health promotion and protection such as family planning and well-baby care. Screening is secondary, and rehabilitation is tertiary.

q: The charge nurse in the long-term-care facility is preparing to deliver an in-service about the secondary level of health care for staff nurses. Which of the following information should the nurse include in the seminar?

q: A nurse is working with an emergency response team caring for a group of people who may have been exposed to anthrax while doing farm work but are not exhibiting manifestations of illness. Select three prescriptions that the nurse would anticipate receiving from the primary health care provider (PHCP).
o: Ciprofloxacin.
Propranolol.
Hydroxychloroquine.
Furosemide.
Doxycycline.
Clindamycin.
r:
Antibiotics are used for anthrax exposure. Ciprofloxacin and doxycycline are the first-line choices and clindamycin is also used in anthrax regimens. Propranolol, hydroxychloroquine, and furosemide do not treat anthrax. Confirm the exact regimen against your class notes.
